posts.name: Gothic_Knight
posts.cooked:
Does Pride's power (to let you use Prejudice's power), supercede the rule that an individual card's power can only be used once per turn?

 

  Ex: Expatriate has in play (and in this order) Tactical Shotgun (Incendiary rounds), Prejudice, Pride, Flack Jacket, and submachine gun.  She plays unload.  My group has decided that all of the powers must be used in the order that the cards were played in, so prejudice goes off before pride does. When pride goes off, can I use Prejudice's ability again?

 

  If so, It means I should make an effort to make sure Prejudice is always in play before I put pride into play.

 

What say you?

 

  Thanks in advance.

posts.name: dpt
posts.cooked:
That's a bizarre choice of your group, to make you use the powers in order, particularly in situations like this.

To answer your question, I don't think Pride should let you override the prohibition against using the same power multiple times, as it doesn't explicitly mention it. (The only case I know that does override it is Mr. Fixer's Overdrive.)

posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked: As others have said: no, Pride won't let you fire Prejudice twice. You can use your guns in any order, and not all the powers you use have to be guns. This does mean that if you have, say, Shotgun, Pride and Prejudice, you can use Load to play Unload, and then use the two powers you get from that on the Shotgun and then Pride... no power left for Prejudice, but Pride lets you fire it anyway, so that's fine :D (It wouldn't work if you fired Pride before the Shotgun though; then Load, Pride and Prejudice would be your three powers used, even if you only fired Prejudice because of Pride.)

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
You can absolutely use Prejudice twice in a single turn. You guys are dropping the ball on the OP here.

Example:

Pride and Prejudice are in play. You play Unload to gain (2) power uses. Use Prejudice first. Then use Pride. Since it specifically and explicitly tells you to use Predudice, you are allowed to do so. 

This is similar to two cases:

1) Overdrive. You can use the same power twice when given explicit instructions to do so

2) Effects that break other base rules, like effects that allow you to play multiple cards during your play phase when the normal rule is play 1 card.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked: On a related note:  If you play Unload with a shotgun in play, and and then use Load to play "Pride", will you be able to fire a gun?  Or to put it another way:  If the number of guns changes after Unload has been played, does the number of available power uses change with it?
posts.raw: On a related note:  If you play Unload with a shotgun in play, and and then use Load to play "Pride", will you be able to fire a gun?  Or to put it another way:  If the number of guns changes after Unload has been played, does the number of available power uses change with it?

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Hmm...personally I would say no because Unload looks at how many guns you have in play at the time it gets played itself - I would see Unload as saying "You can use X powers this turn, whre X the number of guns currently in your play area". If you only had one gun at the time, you would only be able to use one power, even if you use that power to put out a second gone - by that point, Unload has been and gone, its one-shot effect already triggered and telling you that you can use one power in your Power phase (because you only had one gun out at the time it was played).

I might be wrong, but that's how I see it, anyway :).
